name: Host research sources first, then the web (proposed)
description: Proposed. A host declares its research and experience search interfaces; a world question goes to them first and to the web only when they do not cover it, and each finding carries its source and an evidence label.
advantages: Uses the strongest evidence the host has; one shape of finding whatever the source; the web stays the fallback.
disadvantages: Each host must declare and maintain its sources; research interfaces are slower than snippets; not built.

name: Findings weighed by a host's evidence-estimation service (proposed)
description: Proposed. As research_sources_first, with each finding passed to a host's evidence-estimation service that returns how strongly the evidence supports it, stated with the answer.
advantages: Calibrated confidence the person can weigh; the same estimate everywhere the product answers.
disadvantages: Depends on a host service and its cost and latency; not every question has an estimate; the specification owner does not plan to bring such evidence operations into this chat (2026-10-28), so it is recorded as an alternative only; not built.

name: Registry plus per-call ablation against the owner metric (proposed)
description: Proposed. Each call is dropped or downgraded in turn and the owner metric is read again on production-shaped cases; budgets are set from the value shown.
advantages: Shows what each call earns and finds cheaper or faster options.
disadvantages: Paid runs per prompt, and only as good as each owner metric; not built.

name: Hysteresis resource guard
description: Samples memory use, free memory and load, pauses new work when a limit is exceeded and resumes only after readings clear, and can wait until the host is fine. Sampling uses the process file system or a library, with limits from code or the environment.
advantages: Hysteresis prevents flapping, and pausing is lossless because unclaimed work stays queued.
disadvantages: Thresholds are manual and host-specific, and the sampler depends on platform facilities that may be absent.

name: Coding agent with the host reach summary and reach judge (built, off by default)
description: The host supplies a reach summary built from the same source as its grounding, and one small question on a stronger tier before planning settles whether the request lives inside the readable sources, outside them or in the world now; the verdict goes into the planner prompt as a fact.
advantages: Built; asks a fact instead of reviewing a decision; cached per turn; inert without a summary.
disadvantages: Off by default; settles reach for reads, not capability questions or claimed acts; adds a serial call before planning; measured on routing only.

name: Coding agent, reach described in the prompt (today)
description: Outside work runs on the coding agent through the deep runner, and the model infers what it can reach from each effector's own description in the planner prompt (the tool catalog's when-to-use text, the host's grounding).
disadvantages: A gap in the descriptions is filled with a plausible capability; no receipt is required before a claim of an outside act; a setting is not read before a blocker is stated.

name: Registered prompt specs with an enforcement test (today)
description: Prompts are declared as PromptSpecs and a test with a shrinking baseline lists the call sites that are not yet registered.
advantages: Built; every registered prompt carries its owner solution, metric and no-em-dash rule.
disadvantages: Not measured; some call sites are still unregistered (the enforcement baseline lists them), there is no ablation, and spend-weighted value is not computed.

name: Via vendor
description: The hub's arm, selected as it is: every model call asks through the vendor caller and the tier chooser measured best for the tier.
advantages: QAR adds no model path of its own, so a change in the hub's path reaches every part at once.
disadvantages: The justification of each call (the prompt spec registry) is measured apart, so a call that is not justified is found by that metric and not refused here.

name: Static price table lookup
description: Holds a snapshot of list prices per million input tokens by provider and model, detects the provider from the environment, falls back to a stated default for unknown models, and estimates bootstrap cost from a token count.
advantages: Simple, offline and instant, and gives a cost estimate before any spend.
disadvantages: Hand-maintained, input tokens only, and stale until someone edits it.

name: Persisted daily token tracker
description: Counts input and output tokens within a UTC day, persists the tally to a JSON file so a restart reloads it, resets at the day boundary, and reports over-limit and a status line. A limit of zero or off disables it.
advantages: Survives restarts and cleanly separates days; opt-in so it never surprises a lane.
disadvantages: Counts tokens, not money, and a deep runner on a subscription is outside the count; a lost usage file resets the day.

name: Snippet-first research with page extraction
description: The planner-facing adapter: concurrent multi-query search deduplicated by address into one terse observation, plus a focused page fetch that extracts main text, keeps only passages relevant to a focus phrase and caps the result. Everything is cached and a hosted fallback can read pages that resist direct extraction. Fetched addresses are checked against private targets.
advantages: Keeps prompt cost low and answers citable, repeats are free, and safe fetching and clean failure make it suitable as the default. Selected because: config_retrieval web_research wiring (QAR_WEB_SEARCH_*)
disadvantages: Quality is bounded by the chosen backend and a relevance heuristic. Pages built on scripts or behind blocks may need the fallback, and cached results can be stale.

name: Web research with the answer's support check (today)
description: World questions are answered from the model's knowledge and snippet-first web research, and the answer check flags claims the turn's reads do not support and rewrites them once with their basis.
advantages: Built; cheap and fast; unsupported claims are hedged rather than asserted.
disadvantages: No evidence-strength label; a host's research sources are not consulted unless wired as a retrieval source or a tool; general knowledge that passes the check is still stated without a source.
